defect: baseline checkpoint EIO on the block-attach bench

rootCause.owner: first-party benchmark instrumentation, not snapshot-chain publication or the container image
rootCause.mechanism: The meter pipes a counted request body through a FixedLengthStream and forwards it to the SDK R2 bridge, which pipes that native stream into a second FixedLengthStream. This composition stalls nonzero request bodies before the binding returns. s3fs exhausts its bounded HTTP attempts and reports EIO at fsync and close. The stall also occurs with the meter window idle and with only five payload bytes.
rootCause.discriminator: Unchanged SDK-shaped workerd control succeeds with the outer observer absent; the old observer stalls both 5-byte and 4-MiB bodies. Removing only its redundant FixedLengthStream restores both cases with exact observed bytes. The deployed same-image 4-MiB control fails in 213254ms; the stream-only fix commits identical-size archive in 4983ms.
rootCause.fix: Use one backpressured counting TransformStream at the incoming request boundary. Preserve Content-Length and leave the one binding FixedLengthStream to the SDK. No s3fs tuning, retries, image change or alternate publication path.
rootCause.confidence: confirmed by local red/control/green and deployed same-image red/green

hypotheses.disposition: confirmed first-party transport composition; not a measured Cloudflare rate or duration limit
s3fs request timeout/retry exhaustion is the consequence, not the root cause; 4-MiB single PUT also fails
hypotheses.measurement: six unfinished nonzero single PUT attempts start about 35000ms apart; zero-byte PUTs complete in 212-245ms; no multipart operation is needed to reproduce

successful zero-byte writes and same-config fixed 4198400-byte write prove binding access. Source 484f6e822 versus 134335736 bench wrangler template differs only at image; account, BACKUP_BUCKET binding, SANDBOX_TRANSPORT and resource limits agree. Generated bucket and Worker names are run-specific. No real R2 credential enters the container.

hypotheses.candidate: multipart part size or total object size handling
hypotheses.measurement: single-PUT 4198400-byte archive fails; five bytes fail in local SDK-shaped bridge. Fixed SDK proxy tests cover empty/single PUT, 5-MiB first multipart part and 17-byte final part with exact totals.

hypotheses.candidate: new squashfuse_ll or block server holds a path or mount
hypotheses.measurement: same digest locally publishes 67112960-byte archive through s3fs to MinIO in 0.138325s with matching SHA256; with squashfuse_ll holding that archive, a second 67112960-byte archive containing a 2-GiB sparse inode publishes in 0.134770s with matching SHA256. Baseline publication precedes any composed block lower.

imageComparison.dockerfile: packages/devbox/block-lower/Dockerfile inherits the exact previous digest and copies only devbox-block-lower and devbox-squashfuse; s3fs remains 1.90
imageComparison.historicalCorrection: The archived 20260912192123 decisive run uses 484f6e822 and published the 64-MiB ladder checkpoint in 24385ms (71864320 archive bytes). It predates the new transport meter and contains no live C3 observation. It is not a same-Worker-code image comparison.
imageComparison.previousImageLiveControl: p20260913102157/observations.json: same current Worker on previous production image fails 64-MiB baseline in 654224ms; 78 multipart part attempts, zero finish, no completion attempt. Image-only regression rejected.

multipartAbortAttribution.originalReceipt: Parent clarified the original two abort calls were an interim report of the transport /ops count, not a separately persisted raw receipt. Final residue was zero objects and zero uploads, a different measurement. The original abort count is reported provenance, not independently reconstructed data.
multipartAbortAttribution.reachablePath: SDK r2EgressHandler dispatches intercepted DELETE with uploadId to handleAbortMultipartUpload, which calls the counted bucket handle abort. Bench teardown's S3 residue cleanup does not traverse this wrapper.
multipartAbortAttribution.sourceMeaning: ParallelMultipartUploadRequest calls AbortMultipartUpload when its parallel part requests fail, before multipart completion. AbortMultipartUpload emits DELETE uploadId. Thus observed abort calls on this wrapper belong to s3fs abandoning failed part transfers, not an R2 object-expiry timer. Original per-request timing beyond the supplied aggregate remains unavailable.

additionalMeterDefect.mechanism: CountingContainerProxy left under-64 operation batches in its own isolate; /ops flushes only the box and API isolates.
additionalMeterDefect.discriminator: The fixed 4-MiB window records a successful 4198400-byte PUT while /ops only reports head:1.
additionalMeterDefect.fix: Flush the proxy tally in request finally, covering both success and failure.
additionalMeterDefect.pin: actual bench proxy test is red without settlement flush and green with it

localCleanup.note: The local publication/hash checks succeeded. Final s3fs unmount returned busy while squashfuse exited; the --rm test container then exited and removed all local mounts. MinIO and the isolated Docker network were explicitly removed.

boundedCells.verdict: publication EIO repaired; requested block-layer acceptance remains refused for separate lifecycle and fallback evidence gaps
boundedCells.c3Reason: After an empty attach reported ready, the first witness-directory exec hit the platform blockConcurrencyWhile reset before the baseline writer. No C3 checkpoint or changed-file attach ran.
boundedCells.sparseQualification: The restored record has no deltaFormat:chunked. Publication used the whole-upper fallback, so no block lower or block-lower-stats.json exists. The timing is a genuinely fresh base+delta attach, not an admitted v2 block-layer result. Counter read failed before file range verification. The fallback reason was logged only to Worker console, which this driver did not capture.
